data.summary: After ADP-migrate-homes, ddflow/infra/proc.py and ddflow/infra/git.py are compatibility shims, which SNAPSHOT the function. ddflow.adapters.git calls ddflow.adapters.proc.run directly (from . import proc as P -> P.run(...)), so a test that monkeypatches ddflow.infra.proc.run rebinds only the shim name and the patch never fires. On main this leaves test_infra_git.py (test_missing_git_is_unavailable, test_timeout_is_unavailable_and_timed_out, test_locale_is_c) and test_shared_files_nonascii.py (test_a_git_that_cannot_run_gives_the_glob_itself, test_a_git_that_times_out_gives_the_glob_itself) red. Fix: re-target those tests' monkeypatches at ddflow.adapters.proc (the module ddflow.adapters.git actually calls).
data.title: infra proc/git shims snapshot run so monkeypatches no longer reach adapters

data.body:
Fixes bug B58595ea20b: After ADP-migrate-homes, ddflow/infra/proc.py and ddflow/infra/git.py are compatibility shims, which SNAPSHOT the function. ddflow.adapters.git calls ddflow.adapters.proc.run directly (from . import proc as P -> P.run(...)), so a test that monkeypatches ddflow.infra.proc.run rebinds only the shim name and the patch never fires. On main this leaves test_infra_git.py (test_missing_git_is_unavailable, test_timeout_is_unavailable_and_timed_out, test_locale_is_c) and test_shared_files_nonascii.py (test_a_git_that_cannot_run_gives_the_glob_itself, test_a_git_that_times_out_gives_the_glob_itself) red. Fix: re-target those tests' monkeypatches at ddflow.adapters.proc (the module ddflow.adapters.git actually calls).

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B58595ea20b --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B58595ea20b --regression-test <test>` first).
data.title: Fix bug B58595ea20b: infra proc/git shims snapshot run so monkeypatches no longer reach adapters

evidence.note: CONFIRMED: monkeypatching the ddflow/infra/proc.py shim's 'run' no longer reaches the proc module ddflow.adapters.git calls. Mechanism: infra/proc.py does 'from ddflow.adapters.proc import *' (a snapshot); adapters/git.py does 'from . import proc as P; P.run(...)'. Refuting observation that mattered: infra_proc.run is adapter_proc.run is True at import, but setattr(infra_proc, run, spy) would not rebind adapter_proc.run. Cheapest test tests/test_infra_git.py::test_locale_is_c: KeyError 'LC_ALL' on unfixed main, passes after re-targeting the monkeypatch to ddflow.adapters.proc.

chunk_findings.detail: `rows` is documented to produce a descriptor-first ordering, but it only partitions catalog rows by `axis` and then iterates them in whatever order `CAT.load().rows` returns. `DESCRIPTOR_FIRST` is never used to sort the gaps or derive dependencies. If the catalog data lists `hooks` before `descriptor` (or `probe` after `hooks`) with `axis="in_agent"`, and a harness has all of those features `unverified`, `rows` returns the `hooks` gap before the `descriptor`/`probe` gaps, so any filing or dependency construction based on this order violates the stated descriptor-first precedence.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parity/gap_tasks.py:38-49

chunk_findings.detail: The test named for unverified rows does not actually check statuses. It compares `GT.by_agent(hs)[h.id]` to features extracted from the same `GT.rows(hs)` result, making the assertion tautological. If `rows` were changed to include `verified` rows, missing rows, or rows not graded `unverified`, this test would still pass because `by_agent` is derived from the same `rows` output. It should validate against `AN.answers(h)` statuses.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_parity_gap_tasks.py:14-20

chunk_findings.detail: `rows` never reads `DESCRIPTOR_FIRST`, so the claimed descriptor-first needs order is not what callers get. Catalog order `orchestrator`/`parity` then `in_agent`/`hooks` is rewritten to hooks then parity; a catalog ordered `probe` then `descriptor` stays probe-first. Needs built from `by_agent` therefore are not descriptor, probe, hooks/mcp/skills, driver, parity.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/parity/gap_tasks.py:35

chunk_findings.detail: A gap is documented as any descriptor answer of `unverified`, but `rows` drops every catalog row whose `axis` is not `in_agent` or `orchestrator`. An unverified row with `axis="probe"` (or `descriptor` / `driver`) never appears in `rows()` or `by_agent()`, so that `(agent, feature)` gap is omitted.

chunk_findings.detail: `test_gaps_are_the_unverified_rows_deduped_by_agent_row` never reads answers. `by_agent` is built only from `rows`, so `not got - {features in gaps}` is true even if every verified row is emitted. The test stays green when the unverified filter is removed.
